page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance from the E2 family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place this instance primarily in the average tier. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2681.48, while multi-core performance falls into the middle 50% at 10764.32. Memory bandwidth tests yield average results, with read-only large block speeds at 69.61 GB/sec and write speeds at 46.34 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark extended instructions tests represent relative weaknesses, scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highmem-8 offers a high-density memory configuration on a cost-effective shared-resource architecture, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained peak CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include database operations, caching layers, and memory-heavy web serving.

Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads. Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU performance, while multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth metrics consistently rank in the average tier. Conversely, multi-threaded decompression and extended instruction sets represent performance bottlenecks, placing in the bottom 25%. Qualitatively, the instance provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-heavy applications by pairing a generous 8.0 GB of RAM per core with a budget-friendly virtualized platform. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive web serving.
